page: Vultr vc2-16c-64gb is a General Purpose virtual server belonging to the Cloud Compute family. It features 16 shared vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled and consists of a 1280 GB NVMe SSD, while no dedicated GPU hardware is present on this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates that the instance delivers average performance across most compute and memory workloads. The stress-ng single-core score of 1451.59 and multi-core score of 21535.52 align with the middle tier of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is measured at 107.12 GB/sec for large block read operations and 53.71 GB/sec for large block write operations. However, single-threaded performance shows some limitations, as evidenced by a poor Geekbench single-core score of 836.0 and a weak gzip compression throughput of 23.39 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded tasks perform adequately, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6565.0 and a bzip3 multi-threaded decompression speed of 66.52 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the vc2-16c-64gb offers a high density of virtualized resources and local NVMe storage, though the shared CPU allocation represents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, predictable compute performance. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications that can tolerate shared CPU scheduling, such as static web serving, which achieved a throughput of 12.01 GB/sec, and database operations, supported by a Passmark database score of 4649.2 and Redis SET performance of 23.04 million operations per second. Other appropriate workloads include software compilation and basic text or image processing.
